name: Order does not matter
why: 4: 1+1+1+1, 1+1+2, 2+2 and 1+3. If you got 7, you counted 1+1+2, 1+2+1 and 2+1+1 as different: loop over the coins on the outside and the amounts on the inside.

name: Cannot be paid
why: 0: only even amounts can be made from 2s.

name: Amount 0
why: 1: pay with no coins at all. This is the base case ways[0] = 1.

name: One coin, exactly
why: 1: the one way is a single 10 coin.

name: Coins in any order
why: 11. The order of the coins in the list does not change the count.

name: A dollar in cents
why: 292: a well-known count of the ways to change a dollar.

name: ₹100,000 in Indian coins and notes
why: A 25-digit number. One list of 100,001 counts, updated once per coin. Memoised recursion fails here: this input needs far more nested calls than Python allows (about 1,000, and only a few hundred with functools.cache in the browser). Fill a table with a loop instead (lesson 3).
